body: Exposed in what way? `$_hidden` is only used for json serialization

The response generated by

``` PHP
$this->set('companies', $this->paginate());
$this->set('_serialize', ['companies']);
```

Includes a "created_by": { "name": "a" ... } where the 'password' field is not shown, if we had set `$paginate['contain'] = 'CreatedBy'`.

If `$paginate['contain'] = 'createdby'`, the response includes the field "CreatedBy": in which all the hidden fields are also shown.
@lorenzo Doesn't it use the auto-generated model by not using the correct association name which doesn't have `hidden` data?

> The hidden fields from the users table are as expected not shown. if i spell CreatedBy a bit different [] All fields, including the hidden ones are included in the result

Please demonstrate that - i.e. show what's happening and in what way it's not what you expect.

I did some digging on this, and because the alias name does not match the association alias, the data is not mapped into an entity. Instead it is left as an array. This is why the hidden field settings are not applied.

The root cause of this issue is that associations are stored in a case-insenstive way. This was done to catch duplicate association definitions more easily. I think ensuring that the contained associations use their correct aliases might be a way to prevent this issue.

issue.title: 3.4: associations with same name

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
This bug occurred recently, unfortunately I had no way to immediately investigate, so I do not know from which version, maybe from 3.4.

I have `Posts` that belong to `PostsCategories` and `Pages` that belong to `PagesCategoriesTable`.

`PostsTable::initialize()`:

       /// ...
        $this->belongsTo('Categories', [
            'foreignKey' => 'category_id',
            'joinType' => 'INNER',
            'className' => 'MeCms.PostsCategories',
        ]);
       /// ...

`PagesTable::initialize()`:

       /// ...
        $this->belongsTo('Categories', [
            'foreignKey' => 'category_id',
            'joinType' => 'INNER',
            'className' => 'MeCms.PagesCategories',
        ]);
       /// ...

So, as you can see, both associations have the same name.  
I already know that this can be confusing, but until recently worked perfectly.

Now what happens?  
I have a cell that lists the post categories (with something like `$this->Posts->Categories->find()`...). Normally, this cell works.
But when the cell is rendered with an action that also uses the page categories (`$this->Pages->Categories->find()`...), this happens:

```
2017-03-13 05:41:12 - Warning (512): Could not render cell - MeCms\Model\Table\PostsTable association "Categories" of type "manyToOne" to "MeCms\Model\Table\PagesCategoriesTable" doesn't match the expected class "MeCms\Model\Table\PostsCategoriesTable". You can't have an association of the same name with a different target "className" option anywhere in your app. [/var/www/quadrifogliopsichiatria.it/vendor/cakephp/cakephp/src/ORM/Association.php, line 420] in [/var/www/quadrifogliopsichiatria.it/vendor/cakephp/cakephp/src/View/Cell.php, line 271]
```

Debugging `$this->Posts->Categories` inside the cell code there are no problems:

```
object(Cake\ORM\Association\BelongsTo) {
	[protected] _validStrategies => [
		(int) 0 => 'join',
		(int) 1 => 'select'
	]
	[protected] _name => 'Categories'
	[protected] _className => 'MeCms.PostsCategories'
	[protected] _bindingKey => null
	[protected] _foreignKey => 'category_id'
	[protected] _conditions => []
	[protected] _dependent => false
	[protected] _cascadeCallbacks => false
	[protected] _sourceTable => object(MeCms\Model\Table\PostsTable) {

		'registryAlias' => 'MeCms.Posts',
		'table' => 'posts',
		'alias' => 'Posts',
		'entityClass' => 'MeCms\Model\Entity\Post',
		'associations' => [
			(int) 0 => 'categories',
			(int) 1 => 'users',
			(int) 2 => 'tags'
		],
		'behaviors' => [
			(int) 0 => 'Timestamp',
			(int) 1 => 'CounterCache'
		],
		'defaultConnection' => 'default',
		'connectionName' => 'default'
	
	}
	[protected] _targetTable => null
	[protected] _joinType => 'INNER'
	[protected] _propertyName => null
	[protected] _strategy => 'join'
	[protected] _finder => 'all'
	[protected] _tableLocator => null
}
```
The problem occurs calling `find ()`.

The problem is [here](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/master/src/ORM/Association.php#L396): `$this->_targetTable` is `PagesCategories`.

I have, however, noticed a peculiar thing: if specifically the class namespace, the problem does not occur. So:

```php
        $this->belongsTo('Categories', [
            'foreignKey' => 'category_id',
            'joinType' => 'INNER',
            'className' => 'MeCms\Model\Table\PostsCategoriesTable',
        ]);
```

This works.

Unfortunately I'm not to say more than that. Is it a bug? How can I help?
